key_features.classic_presentation: Acute mesenteric ischemia presents with SUDDEN ONSET SEVERE PERIUMBILICAL PAIN (9-10/10) that is OUT OF PROPORTION to physical exam findings (severe pain but minimal tenderness). Classic presentation: 'PAIN OUT OF PROPORTION'. Pain is CONSTANT, crampy or colicky initially, becoming steady. Onset is acute, within hours. Occurs almost exclusively in patients >60 years with vascular disease. Key associated symptoms: BLOODY DIARRHEA (late finding), nausea, vomiting, urgent bowel movements. Patient appears in severe distress despite benign abdominal exam initially. Location: Diffuse, periumbilical. Key history: ATRIAL FIBRILLATION (embolic source), peripheral vascular disease, prior MI, hypercoagulable state. Classic triad: severe pain + minimal findings + elderly with vascular disease. Key positives: Severe pain with soft abdomen early, bloody diarrhea (late), metabolic acidosis. Key negatives: Young patient without vascular disease makes mesenteric ischemia extremely unlikely.

red_flags: EMERGENCY CONDITION - severe pain out of proportion to exam in elderly with AFib - call 911 immediately
Bloody diarrhea with severe pain - bowel infarction, needs immediate vascular surgery
Peritoneal signs developing - bowel necrosis/perforation, fatal without emergency surgery
Metabolic acidosis with elevated lactate - tissue ischemia, extremely poor prognosis without immediate intervention
